one_line: Verified: 34 dated Inside Airbnb Barcelona snapshots committed under data/original/airbnb/<YYMMDD>/ from 150430 (30 Apr 2015) to 190308 (8 Mar 2019), each with listings_summary_barcelona_insideairbnb.csv (~2.0-3.0 MB; columns id, host_id, neighbourhood, lat/lon, room_type, price, minimum_nights, number_of_reviews, last_review, reviews_per_month, calculated_host_listings_count, availability_365) and reviews_summary_barcelona_insideairbnb.csv (listing_id+date, 2.9 MB in 2015 rising to 11.1 MB in 2019); repo ~147 MB total, plus boundary shapefiles and Barcelona population/dwelling tables; no LICENSE file (upstream Inside Airbnb is CC BY 4.0); last push 19 Oct 2019, 0 stars, not archived.
abnb_use: Direct hit on gap #1 (Inside Airbnb dumps older than ~1 year, which are off the CDN): 34 pre-2023 Barcelona vintages give a 2015-2019 base period for the reviews-based stays index, host-concentration and quoted-price/availability series in one of our 13 panel cities, and let the 2022-2026 EMEA nights/ADR trend be judged against a full pre-COVID cycle and the 2016-17 Barcelona HUTB crackdown.
sample_plan: cd <scratch>; D=https://raw.githubusercontent.com/montera34/airbnb.barcelona/master/data/original/airbnb; for d in 150430 160103 170104 180117 190308; do curl -sL -o bcn_listings_$d.csv "$D/$d/listings_summary_barcelona_insideairbnb.csv"; done  (5 files, ~12.5 MB); then curl -sL -o bcn_reviews_190308.csv "$D/190308/reviews_summary_barcelona_insideairbnb.csv" (11.1 MB, cumulative review history back to 2009). Total ~24 MB, under the cap. Record the full 34-date list with `gh api repos/montera34/airbnb.barcelona/contents/data/original/airbnb --jq '.[].name'` and note remaining dates for a later targeted pull. Do NOT run anything in scraping/.
reasoning: Verified by gh api: the 34 dated snapshot directories and both CSVs per date really are committed, with prices and availability in the listings summary and full review dates in the reviews summary. This is exactly the pre-2023 Inside Airbnb history the CDN no longer serves, for a city already in our panel, so it extends rather than duplicates what we hold. No repo licence is stated, so redistribution outside the team needs a human call; the underlying data is Inside Airbnb under CC BY 4.0.

one_line: Verified: Chen & Zimmermann open-source cross-sectional asset pricing - ~15,000 lines of Python (signal construction) and R (portfolio construction) for 200+ published anomalies including EarningsSurprise/SUE, GPL-2.0, 1,043 stars, actively maintained (last push 22 Oct 2025). No data is committed: signals and portfolio returns are distributed off-repo at https://www.openassetpricing.com/data/ via Google Drive (monthly long-short returns for 212 predictors as a wide CSV; stock-level signals ~1.6 GB zipped; coverage through Dec 2024, option-IV signals through Dec 2022), also reachable via `pip install openassetpricing` or the R package OpenSourceAP.DownloadR. Rebuilding from source needs WRDS credentials and a FRED API key.
abnb_use: Gap #17 methods: the monthly long-short return series for the EarningsSurprise/SUE family gives a market-wide base rate for post-earnings drift, i.e. whether a drift trade around the 5 Nov ABNB print has any unconditional edge before we build one, and the wider signal set is a ready benchmark for any factor attribution on an ABNB position.
sample_plan: Not to be pulled by an agent. If a human wants it: the monthly long-short portfolio returns CSV (small, ~212 predictors x monthly since 1926-2024) from https://www.openassetpricing.com/data/ (Google Drive), or `pip install openassetpricing` then pull only the portfolio-return table; never the 1.6 GB stock-level signal archive, and never the WRDS rebuild path.
reasoning: Real, large, actively maintained project, but nothing usable is in git - the code needs WRDS (paid subscription) plus a FRED key, and the data lives on Google Drive, outside the hosts an agent may pull from, with the biggest file at 1.6 GB. Cataloguing it with the exact data-page URL is the right outcome; a human can decide whether to take the small monthly long-short return file.
